Portrait 3:4 composition. Title: "Wallet recovery". Three numbered sections stacked vertically, separated by whitespace and horizontal rules, each with a short, internally vertical or compact wrapped process. Section 1 heading "1. Make a reusable key". Sequence "Private wallet signature" → "HKDF-SHA-256" → "X25519 key pair". From key pair show two labeled branches "Private key stays in memory" and "Public card goes to creator". Section 2 heading "2. Protect the backup". Box "Random file key" has two distinct branches: one to "Encrypt backup · AES-256-GCM"; the other to "Shamir split · 3 of 5" then "Encrypt each share for its custodian". Section 3 heading "3. No cross-section arrows that would falsely imply a public card turns into a random file key. Use simple accurate boxes and directed connectors.
title: Wallet recovery protocol
alt: A fixed private wallet signature passes through HKDF-SHA-256 to derive an X25519 key pair. The creator uses a fresh random file key to encrypt the backup and splits that key into five Shamir shares, encrypting one for each custodian. During recovery, custodians recreate their derived recovery keys, open any three distinct shares, rebuild the file key, and decrypt the backup.

(2) In the bottom-left process box replace 'Recreate wallet keys' with 'Recreate recovery keys' because these are signature-derived recovery keys, not the Ethereum signing keys. Preserve the font style and fit the words neatly inside that box. No other changes.
